source_resources.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
source_resources.author: Timo Schick, Jane Dwivedi-Yu, Roberto Dessì, Roberta Raileanu, Maria Lomeli, Luke Zettlemoyer, Nicola Cancedda, Thomas Scialom
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Sections 2-3: API-call annotation, sampling, filtering, tool integration
source_resources.license: arXiv.org perpetual non-exclusive license / Open Access
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic reference under arXiv open access terms.
source_resources.prerequisites: Language-model finetuning, API calls, and tool schemas.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Primary reference for model-tool integration with explicit API contracts; informs the capstone's adapter boundary where the harness owns tool validation and the model only proposes calls.
source_resources.safe_fallback: The capstone's tool contract template (name, typed arguments, error modes) is fully specified in the lesson instructions.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Prompt-time interleaving rather than finetuned tool calls; both define the model-side of the same adapter boundary.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Patil et al.: Gorilla: Large Language Model Connected with Massive APIs
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Large API-corpus retrieval; Toolformer's minimal single-tool mechanics match the capstone's bounded tool set.

source_resources.title: LLM Powered Autonomous Agents
source_resources.author: Lilian Weng
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Sections: planning, memory, tool use, challenges
license_restrictions: Prose is linked, not copied; the curriculum uses its own bounded-agent implementation
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external hyperlink to a publicly published research blog; no text imported.
source_resources.prerequisites: Agent loops, tool use, and planning vocabulary.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Widely used survey mapping agent architecture components (planning, memory, tools) and their failure modes; supports the capstone integration architecture review.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Personal blog; availability depends on the author's hosting.
source_resources.safe_fallback: The capstone architecture lesson specifies the adapter boundary, budgets, and tool contracts directly; no blog content is required offline.

compared_candidates.license: MIT License (outside autogpt_platform/); Polyform Shield License (autogpt_platform/)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Open-ended autonomous loop; deliberately excluded as the capstone must remain a bounded, evaluable system.
Task-list autonomy demo; the survey article gives vocabulary while the capstone keeps fixed tasks and budgets.

source_resources.title: OpenAI Evals: Framework for Evaluating LLMs and Contamination Checks
source_resources.author: OpenAI Research
source_resources.permission_basis: Permissive open source reference under MIT license.
source_resources.prerequisites: Python, evaluation harnesses (MMLU, GSM8K), JSONL datasets.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Standardized evaluation repository specifying rigorous separation of eval prompts, canary GUID strings, and contamination test protocols.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Canary GUID matching, token set intersection, and leak detection scripts are implemented in the curriculum.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Widely adopted evaluation harness; OpenAI Evals provides explicit canary guidance and contamination check specifications.
Modern lightweight eval framework; OpenAI Evals illustrates standard test-set integrity guarantees.

source_resources.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
source_resources.author: Noah Shinn, Federico Cassano, Ashwin Gopinath, Karthik Narasimhan, Shunyu Yao
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Sections 3-4: self-reflection loop, episodic memory, retry budgets
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic reference under arXiv open access terms.
source_resources.prerequisites: Agent loops, tool feedback, and retry semantics.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Defines failure-feedback-driven retry with bounded attempts; justifies the capstone's retry budget and its distinction between corrected-in-budget and safe termination.
source_resources.safe_fallback: The fault-injection drill specifies verdict classes and budgets locally without needing the paper.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Single-episode action/observation protocol; Reflexion adds the cross-attempt self-correction used in the recovery drill.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Gou et al.: CRITIC: Large Language Models Can Self-Correct with Tool-Interactive Critiquing
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: External-tool critiquing loop; Reflexion's verbal-feedback retry is simpler to bind to the capstone's retry budget.

activities.title: Controlled Delivery: CI Checks and Rollback Rehearsal

source_resources.title: Continuous Integration
source_resources.author: Martin Fowler
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Practices of Continuous Integration: Make the Build Self-Testing; Fix Broken Builds Immediately
license_restrictions: Article is linked, not copied; pipeline practice uses the repository's own runner
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external hyperlink to a publicly published essay; no text imported.
source_resources.prerequisites: Version control, automated tests, and build scripts.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Standard essay defining CI as verified mainline integration; grounds the capstone delivery rehearsal's check-before-merge and broken-build-response rules.
source_resources.safe_fallback: scripts/ci_practice_runner.py demonstrates each stage locally; the article is a reference, not a dependency.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Full deployment-pipeline book; the Fowler essay suffices for the rehearsal vocabulary while the repo runner supplies practice.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Forsgren, Humble, Kim: Accelerate / DORA State of DevOps
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Industry metrics research; cited as background while the article supplies the operative CI definition.

source_resources.title: Site Reliability Engineering, Chapter 8: Release Engineering
source_resources.author: Dinah McNutt (ed. Betsy Beyer, Tim Harvey), in Site Reliability Engineering (eds. Betsy Beyer, Chris Jones, Jennifer Petoff, Niall Richard Murphy; Google)
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Chapter 8: release pipeline, canarying, rollback criteria
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external hyperlink under the book's published Creative Commons terms; no text imported into proprietary material.
source_resources.prerequisites: Version control, CI basics, and deployment vocabulary.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Defines staged rollout, health-gated release, and rollback criteria; supplies the controlled-deployment and health-failure stages rehearsed by the capstone.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Freely readable on sre.google; print edition is commercial.
source_resources.safe_fallback: The CI practice runner encodes the same stages in disposable fixtures, so the exercise is self-contained.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: General delivery pipeline text; the SRE chapter adds explicit rollback/health-gate criteria used by the drill.
Integration-side discipline; the SRE chapter covers the release and rollback side of the same rehearsal.
